caption_used: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline MistralV0.2-Base and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. The chart displays six specialty groups along the x-axis (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics), with the y-axis showing negative log probability ranging from approximately -27 to -22. Within each group, the MistralV0.2-Base bar (light blue) consistently shows the highest negative log probability, indicating weaker token predictions at baseline. Among the fine-tuned models, the Gastro-tuned variant achieves the lowest negative log probability across most specialty groups, suggesting strong cross-specialty transfer. Notably, the Infect group shows the largest overall bar heights, with baseline reaching approximately -23.5, while the Cardio group exhibits the smallest spread between baseline and fine-tuned variants at roughly 1.5 units.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION:This bar chart illustrates the negative log probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between a baseline language model (MistralV0.2-Base) and the same model fine-tuned on data from six medical specialties. The horizontal axis represents the per-specialty terms, labeled Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics, listed in that order. The vertical axis displays the negative log probability, labeled “Negative log probability”, with a linear scale ranging from approximately -27 to -22, with tick marks at intervals of 1. For each specialty, there are two bars: a light blue bar representing the MistralV0.2-Base model and an orange bar representing the fine-tuned model for that specialty. The bars are grouped side-by-side for each specialty. The light blue bars consistently have higher negative log probability values than the corresponding orange bars within each specialty group, with values ranging from approximately -23 to -26. The orange bars, representing the fine-tuned models, generally have lower negative log probability values, ranging from approximately -24 to -25.5. The “Infect” specialty exhibits the tallest bars overall, with the baseline model reaching a negative log probability of approximately -23.5, while the “Cardio” specialty shows the smallest difference in height between the baseline and fine-tuned bars, with a spread of roughly 1.5 units. No bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, outlining, or annotations.
